title.narrative: Number of Communication and Visibility Training Event

description.narrative: Number of Communication and Visibility Training Event

comment.narrative: In accordance with the initial project ToR the delivery of one 1 two days longtraining for at least 50 of which at least 50 are women including practical examples and interactive sessions with participants and two 2 visibility events in Kosovo with at least 100 participants of which at least 50 are women were foreseen.

At the early stage of the project implementation the Communication and Visibility NKE drafted the Report with the Findings related to the currently existing Communication and Visibility Plans of the grant beneficiaries applied under relevant actions namely objectives activities evaluation and resources. In addition the CV NKE has compiled the following outputs related to the communication and visibility aspects i. Communication and Visibility Plan Template and ii. Good ExamplesLessons Learned and Best Practices on Communication and Visibility in line with EU Visibility and Communication Rules. These reports provided CSOs with the necessary tools and resources to ensure successful communication and visibility of their projects including training templates and coaching on EU communication and visibility rules as well as have improved the transparency and image of EU support to civil societies in Kosovo. The establishment of a communication and visibility helpdesk was a critical component in the successful implementation of the Project. The helpdesk served as the central hub for grantees seeking guidance on how to effectively implement their visibility and communication plans and on how to ensure compliance with EU visibility guidelines. This helpdesk was established on the 1st of February 2022. The project team successfully conducted a highly interactive and engaging twoday online training on Effective Communication and EU Visibility Requirements in partnership with EU Resource Centre and Kosovo Civil Society Foundation. The training utilized the latest technology to deliver an impactful learning experience for participants. This twodays training was conducted on the 1st of November 2021 and respectively 2nd of November 2021 via the use of online platform Zoom. It equipped participants with valuable skills and knowledge in communication and visibility planning online and offline communication information campaigns events and stakeholder engagement print communication coordination between grantees and more.Apart from the above the KLSC Project Team organized an additional twodays workshop on Learning the Basics of the EU visibility guidelines. This twoday training workshop was conducted on the 7th and 8th of December 2022 in the EU Resource Centre Kosovo Civil Society Foundation premises. It was focused on defining the basics of communicating and raising EU visibility explaining the EU strategic communications requirements informing the participants about the legal and contractual obligations explaining the main differences between the old and the new guidelines by providing practical examples and a walkthrough case studies and relevant resources regarding visibility requirements. The KLSC Project Team in close collaboration with TACSO KCSF EUOK and Europe House successfully designed and coordinated a series of initiatives aimed at increasing public awareness about the work of civil society and media in Kosovo as well as raising visibility for the EUs ongoing cooperation and assistance to the sectors supported by CSF and EIDHR projects. With a goal of effectively communicating the benefits of their work to the public the team carefully designed and planned a highimpact twodays visibility and communication event each showcasing the contributions of civil society and media in their own unique way. This twodays public event was held on the 16th and 17th of June 2022 at the amphitheater of Zahir Pajaziti square.

title.narrative: Number of Gender Equality and GAP III Training Event

description.narrative: Number of Gender Equality and GAP III Training Event

comment.narrative: The initial project ToR did not foresee the delivery of a training on the gender issues and EU GAP III.

As mentioned above the objective of the training was to equip CSOs with a better understanding of the EU GAP III and enable them to analyze genderrelated problems and requirements effectively. This allowed them to tailor their project plans accordingly and provide a more comprehensive response to the gender issues. This training was organized at the premises of KCSF on the 13th of July 2023.

title.narrative: Number of focus groups

description.narrative: Number of focus groups

comment.narrative: At the projects inception phase we have foreseen to conduct 2 focus group sessions to gather user insights and feedback. These sessions aimed to identify user needs and challenges enabling us to propose new and improved features to enhance the platform. The insights gathered would help ensure the platforms continuous and active usage by aligning updates with user expectations and making the platform more engaging and userfriendly.

The two planned focus group sessions were successfully held on January 24 2024 and January 29 2024. These sessions provided valuable insights into user needs and preferences enabling us to propose new improved features for the platform.

title.narrative: Number of relevant documents analysed

description.narrative: Number of relevant documents analysed

comment.narrative: At the start of the project several key documents were identified for analysis to understand the current state and operational requirements of the platform. These included the Terms of Reference ToR of the project the assessment report on the CSD platforms operational features the technical documentagreement on the establishment of the platform accessible on the platforms admin page as well as brief screening reports on both the 1st and 2nd platform upgrades accompanied by detailed lists of modifications.

During the inception phase all identified documents were thoroughly analyzed. The insights gained from this analysis have been crucial in guiding platform enhancements and aligning its functionality with project goals and user requirements.

comment.narrative: During the inception phase the project planned to develop a prototype to showcase potential improvements to the CSD platform. This prototype aimed to visualize the proposed upgrades allowing stakeholders to review and provide feedback on key features and functionalities before full implementation.

The prototype was successfully presented to beneficiaries serving as a valuable preview of the planned upgrades for the CSD platform. This prototype allowed beneficiaries to grasp the key elements envisioned for improvement during the implementation phase acting as a visual guide that illustrated upcoming changes and enhancements.
